situation_summary: US-Israeli strikes on Iran on 28 February 2026 set off a regional war. Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz, and it has not reopened to normal traffic, cutting off most Gulf oil and LNG exports; the IEA calls it the largest supply disruption in oil-market history. Retaliatory strikes damaged Gulf energy assets: Qatar lost ~17% of its LNG capacity for 3-5 years at Ras Laffan, Israel hit South Pars, and Saudi (Ras Tanura, SAMREF, Abqaiq, Jazan), Emirati (Fujairah, Shah, Habshan) and Kuwaiti (Mina al-Ahmadi) facilities were hit. An 8 April ceasefire and a 17 June US-Iran MoU briefly revived traffic and pushed oil back to pre-war levels, but the truce collapsed on 7-8 July. Since then the US has blockaded Iranian ports (from 14 July), Iran runs a permit-and-toll regime, and tanker attacks continue. The second front is the Red Sea: the Houthis declared a ban on Saudi shipping from 20 July, struck tankers and the Jazan refinery, and seized Mocha on 10 September. Drones from Iraq hit Abqaiq (27 July) and shut the East-West bypass pipeline (10-11 September), which restarted at reduced rates around 22 September; Saudi Arabia has offset the outage by selling roughly 60 million barrels for ship-to-ship transfer at Sohar, Oman, pushing STS capacity there and at Fujairah to its limit and tightening the VLCC market. In the Black Sea, Ukrainian strikes on Russian ports and refineries (Baltic ports in March, Novorossiysk/CPC, Tuapse, Moscow) and Turkey's 8 August permit halt for Novorossiysk-bound ships have cut flows. Policy responses include a record 400 mb IEA stock release (US 172 mb), the UAE's exit from OPEC (1 May) and US consideration of diesel export curbs. US LNG exports are at records as new trains start up (Golden Pass, Corpus Christi Stage 3), and Panama Canal and Trans Mountain flows to Asia have risen. As of 25 September Brent was $104.32 (pre-crisis ~$72.5) and TTF ~€72/MWh (pre-crisis ~€32). Iran offered at the UN to reopen the strait within a week if the US lifted its naval blockade; Trump rejected the offer on 26 September but told Axios on 27 September that he expects US-Iran talks, mediated by Qatar, to resume as soon as this week.

He said Iran wants a deal the US might have accepted about a year ago and has 'overplayed its hand'; US and Iranian positions remain far apart on the naval blockade, strait reopening and Iran's nuclear program.

The extra volume has pushed Sohar and Fujairah STS operations close to their capacity limits and tightened the VLCC market; analysts estimate the higher Saudi flows require 36-40 additional VLCCs.

sources.name: The Moscow Times (citing Reuters) — Ukrainian drone strikes halt at least 40% of Russia's oil export capacity

events.title: QatarEnergy declares long-term force majeure; 17% of capacity out for 3-5 years
events.summary: QatarEnergy declared force majeure on long-term LNG contracts with buyers in Italy, Belgium, South Korea and China. The 19 March strikes damaged two of 14 LNG trains and a GTL plant, removing 12.8 mtpa (~17% of export capacity); repairs are estimated at 3-5 years and lost revenue at ~$20bn a year.

sources.name: Al Jazeera — QatarEnergy declares force majeure on some LNG contracts due to Iran war
Fox Business — QatarEnergy declares force majeure after Iran strikes on Ras Laffan facility

events.title: Iraq declares force majeure on foreign-operated fields as Basra exports halt
events.summary: Iraq's oil ministry declared force majeure on 20 March on fields operated by foreign companies after ordering shutdowns on 17 March; Basra Oil Company cut output from ~3.3 mb/d to ~0.9 mb/d with southern exports halted by the Hormuz closure. Rumaila had already cut up to 700 kb/d.

sources.name: Middle East Forum — What does Iraq's force majeure declaration mean for energy markets?

events.title: Iran strikes Ras Laffan, SAMREF, Habshan and Kuwaiti refineries
events.summary: In retaliation for the South Pars strike, Iran hit Qatar's Ras Laffan complex (extensive damage), UAE's Habshan gas facility and Bab field, Saudi Arabia's SAMREF refinery at Yanbu, and Kuwait's Mina al-Ahmadi and Mina Abdullah refineries (Mina al-Ahmadi was hit again on 20 March). Brent rose above $110.

sources.name: OPB/NPR — Israel and Iran attack gas facilities in a major escalation that rattles markets
Al Jazeera — QatarEnergy declares force majeure on some LNG contracts due to Iran war

events.title: Iranian missile damages infrastructure serving Haifa's Bazan refinery
events.summary: An Iranian missile hit the Haifa Bay area, damaging third-party infrastructure essential to the Bazan refinery; most production remained active and restoration was expected to take a few days.

sources.name: Times of Israel — Haifa refinery says more missile attack damage found near site, but most production online

events.title: Israel strikes South Pars gas processing at Asaluyeh
events.summary: Israel struck gas treatment facilities at Asaluyeh serving the South Pars field, which supplies about 70% of Iran's domestic gas, triggering Iranian retaliation against Gulf energy infrastructure. Trump said the US 'knew nothing' in advance and threatened South Pars if attacks on Qatar continued.

sources.name: OPB/NPR — Israel and Iran attack gas facilities in a major escalation that rattles markets
Al Jazeera — QatarEnergy declares force majeure on some LNG contracts due to Iran war

events.title: Iraq restarts crude exports via Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline
events.summary: Iraq and the Kurdistan Regional Government resumed exports through the Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline to Turkey on 18 March at ~250 kb/d, with up to 200 kb/d more possible. Iraqi output had fallen to ~1.4 mb/d from ~4.2 mb/d and southern exports (3.4 mb/d pre-war) were halted.

sources.name: The National — Iraq resumes crude oil exports to Turkey's Ceyhan port through pipeline

events.title: Drone strikes halt ADNOC crude loadings at Fujairah; Shah gas field shut
events.summary: Drone strikes and fires at Fujairah on 14 and 16 March halted loadings of ADNOC Murban crude (normally over 1 mb/d) at the UAE's only export outlet outside Hormuz; the port kept operating at reduced capacity. A drone attack also shut the Shah sour-gas field, which supplies at least 500 MMcf/d.

sources.name: Cyprus Mail (Reuters) — Attacks on UAE's Fujairah port, Shah gas field add to energy disruptions

events.title: US strikes 90 military targets on Kharg Island, spares oil terminal
events.summary: CENTCOM struck about 90 military targets on Kharg Island, including mine and missile storage, while deliberately sparing the terminal that handles ~90% of Iran's crude exports. Iran warned it would destroy regional oil and gas infrastructure if its own were hit.

sources.name: NBC News — U.S. bombing of Kharg Island, Iran's critical oil hub, sparks new threats

events.title: IEA agrees record 400 mb emergency stock release; US to release 172 mb
events.summary: All 32 IEA members agreed a 400 million barrel collective stock release, the largest ever and the sixth in IEA history. The US announced a 172 million barrel contribution from its Strategic Petroleum Reserve and Japan about 80 million barrels. The IEA has called the disruption the largest in the history of the oil market.

events.title: QatarEnergy halts LNG production after attacks; TTF jumps 46%
events.summary: QatarEnergy halted production after military attacks on Ras Laffan and Mesaieed industrial cities. Qatar supplies about 20% of world LNG. Dutch TTF front-month rose €14.52 to €46.52/MWh on 2 March from about €32 the previous Friday.

sources.name: Al Jazeera — QatarEnergy declares force majeure on some LNG contracts due to Iran war
RTÉ — European gas prices surge by 46% after QatarEnergy move

events.title: Aramco shuts Ras Tanura refinery after drone attack
events.summary: Aramco shut its 550 kb/d Ras Tanura refinery after a drone attack caused a fire, with a temporary halt in loadings reported; the Saudi energy ministry said the damage came from debris of intercepted drones. Brent rose to about $80.

sources.name: The National — Saudi Aramco shuts down Ras Tanura refinery due to 'drone attack'

events.title: US-Israeli strikes on Iran; IRGC declares Strait of Hormuz closed
events.summary: After US-Israeli strikes that killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, the IRGC broadcast that no ship may pass the strait; by 2 March it limited passage to Iran-approved vessels. Major carriers suspended transits and war-risk premiums jumped. Before the war about 20 mb/d of oil (around a quarter of seaborne oil trade) and almost 20% of global LNG trade passed through Hormuz (IEA, based on Kpler). Israel shut the Leviathan and Karish gas fields as a precaution.
